answer: Land is the gate: an identity is recognised only if it holds a knoll, and the falcon that keeps the land registry rents each title at one juniper times the number of titles its holder owns, due every epoch and eaten by the falcon. One title costs one juniper; the second makes both cost two; a thousand titles cost a thousand each, so an operator running a thousand identities pays a million juniper an epoch, where a single holder pays one. The registry tallies funding roots, so a fresh purse does not restart the count.
